title: Stamp 3: The Boom and Magical Realism
welcome_lead: Stamp the Latin American Boom and magical realism.
meta_desc: A-Level Spanish adventure on the Boom latinoamericano, Garcia Marquez, Vargas Llosa, and magical realism.

concepts.def: Literary boom of the 1960s-70s when Latin American novels gained worldwide fame.
Magical realism; narrative style where the magical is presented as natural.
Colombian author (1927-2014); Nobel Prize 1982; Cien anos de soledad (1967).
Peruvian author (1936-2025); Nobel Prize 2010; La ciudad y los perros (1963).
Argentine author (1914-1984); Rayuela (1963), Boom-era experimental novel.
Mexican author (1928-2012); La muerte de Artemio Cruz (1962).

walkthroughs.body_html: The Boom emerged in the 1960s through novels that mixed experimentation with political themes. Barcelona publisher Carlos Barral and agent Carmen Balcells helped bring authors to international audiences.
Garcia Marquez's Cien anos de soledad (1967) traces seven generations of the Buendia family in Macondo. Magical and historical elements intermingle; over 50 million copies have been sold.
Nobel Prizes for Boom authors: Asturias (1967, Guatemala), Garcia Marquez (1982, Colombia), Paz (1990, Mexico), Vargas Llosa (2010, Peru). Their global recognition transformed Hispanic literature.
